title: Adaptive provider binding and cache-hit overhead attribution
motivation: Production-shaped serialized reference-floor timing preserves fidelity but shows only 1.56% median CPU reduction, much less than isolated self-built Richards timing. The backend currently rebinds adaptive hydraulics on every prescribed-head physical advance.
question: How much runtime is spent re-acquiring an already-built adaptive table and rebuilding binding metadata compared with reusing an already-bound immutable table/provider state?
current_hot_path: bind analytical fallback for current step duration
construct one-node sampler parameter set from 42 initialized coefficients
construct exact cache key and fingerprint
scan cache and copy/acquire existing table

experiments.A: Warm-cache bind microbenchmark: repeatedly call bind_b110_adaptive_hydraulic_provider with identical authority and step duration; report time per bind and cache-stat deltas.
experiments.B: Warm-provider constitutive benchmark: evaluate an already-bound adaptive provider over representative heads; report time per provider evaluation.
experiments.C: Reference-floor cache accounting: record cache hit/build/miss deltas over a fixed number of repeated adaptive floor samples to prove whether one cache acquisition occurs per physical advance.

decision_rule.binding_overhead_actionable: warm-cache binding cost is material relative to one Richards physical advance and cache-hit count scales approximately one-for-one with repeated advances
decision_rule.binding_overhead_not_primary: warm-cache binding cost is too small to explain the observed loss of end-to-end speed

repair_boundary_if_actionable: Memoize immutable table acquisition by exact hydraulic key and policy version.
Do not memoize step-dependent analytical fallback semantics incorrectly.
